body:
Closing this — **the report was wrong, and the fault is mine.** There is no bug here.

The reference inputs are not passed as a nested object. In an API-format prompt they
are **flat, dotted keys**, indexed from `0`:

```json
"ref_audios.ref_audio_0": ["20", 0],
"ref_images.ref_image_0": ["21", 0]
```

not

```json
"ref_audios": {"ref_audio_1": ["20", 0]}
```

This is visible in the shipped template `video_minimax_h3_r2v.json`, where the inputs
are named `ref_images.ref_image_0` / `ref_audios.ref_audio_0`, and in `execution.py`,
which regroups those dotted keys through `_io.build_nested_inputs()` before calling
`execute()`.

My key `ref_audios` matched no declared input, so it was dropped — which is exactly
why four runs produced bit-identical audio. Re-running the same graph, same seed, same
files, with the dotted form changes the output immediately:

| syntax | MD5 of decoded PCM |
|---|---|
| nested (wrong) | `362b9ef3ceaaf0fd6cd45abb18622d8e` |
| no references at all | `362b9ef3ceaaf0fd6cd45abb18622d8e` |
| **dotted, from the official template** | `1d8b28e58a8f3c00f616176dd6ea42e4` |

Reference conditioning works. Sorry for the noise.

The one thing I would still gently raise, as a suggestion rather than a bug: an unknown
key in a node's inputs is dropped silently. A warning naming the ignored key would have
saved this whole investigation. Happy to open that as a separate feature request if it
sounds useful — but this issue as written is incorrect and should not stay open.
